`test.describe.configure()` now accepts a `lock` option, either one lock name or an array of names. It takes the same form as `lock` in test details. I haven't built or run anything, so this is untested.

- **Behavior:** `_configure` in `packages/playwright/src/common/testType.ts` validates the value with `validateTestDetails`, so bad values give the same errors as in test details. It then adds the locks to the suite that is currently loading. That suite can be the file itself or a `describe` group.
- **Inheritance:** I made no change here. `suiteUtils.ts` already copies each parent suite's `_locks` onto its tests, so every test in the file or group takes the lock, including tests in nested groups.
- **Group-scoped fixture overrides:** The call goes through the public API, so a wrapper around a `test.use` override can call `test.describe.configure({ lock })` inside the group. The lock then covers only that group.
- **Types and docs:** I added `lock?: string | string[]` to the `configure` signature in `packages/playwright/types/test.d.ts`. I also documented the new option in `docs/src/test-api/class-test.md`. If `test.d.ts` is generated from the docs, running the repo's doc generation will confirm the two stay in sync.

If the same lock is set at several levels, it ends up in a test's lock list more than once. I didn't deduplicate, and I haven't checked whether the scheduler copes with duplicate names.
